# `pq topic purge`

> CLI reference, PaderQueue 4.x

Purges a topic.

## Usage
```
pq topic purge <name> [flags]
```

## Flags
| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--since` | Only consider objects created after this timestamp (ISO 8601). |
| `--include-internal` | Also show internal system objects (names starting with `__`). |
| `--output` | Output format: `table`, `json` or `yaml`. Default: `table`. |

## Example
```
pq topic purge orders --since
```

Title: PQ-E2187 PARTITIONER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED
Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E2187 PARTITIONER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `partitioner: buffer exhausted`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
The in-memory buffer of the partitioner is full and new data is rejected.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Reduce the incoming rate or increase `partitioner.buffer_bytes`. Also check whether downstream processing is stuck.

Title: Postmortem INC-2024-189
Type: incident
Version: 4.x

# Postmortem INC-2024-189: billing-events degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 140 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `billing-events`

## Summary
During the incident, `billing-events` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E2187 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `billing-events` fired.
- T+35: On-call engineer found PQ-E2187 in the broker logs.
- T+70: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+140: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E2187.
- Add an alert for this error code.

Title: partitioner.buffer_bytes
Type: config
Version: 4.x

# `partitioner.buffer_bytes`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Size of the in-memory buffer used by the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, in bytes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer (bytes) |
| Default | `16777216` |
| Available since | 2.0 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Unit | bytes |
| Default changed | in 3.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `partitioner.buffer_bytes` only if you observe problems with the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
buffer_bytes = 16777216
```

Title: PaderQueue 1.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 1.1

option `retention.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period starts throttling. - New error code PQ-E1547 (PARTITIONER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `partitioner.enabled`: turns the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written on or off.

- New option `scheduler.log_level`: log verbosity of the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time.

- New option `quota.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E4798 (SCHEDULER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `acktracker.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `snapshotter.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues.

- New error code PQ-E4663 (COORDINATOR_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `auth.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the authentication module that validates client tokens.

- New option `broker.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues.

- New error code PQ-E3805 (DLQ_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E2547 (COMPACTOR_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- T+25: Service recovered.

- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E1565.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# PQ-E3642 ACKTRACKER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `acktracker: work queue full`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
The internal work queue of the acktracker is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `acktracker.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

# `auth.max_retries` (PaderQueue 3.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Maximum number of retry attempts of the authentication module that validates client tokens before an operation is reported as failed.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `20` |
| Available since | 2.3 |
| Component | auth |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `auth.max_retries` only if you observe problems with the authentication module that validates client tokens, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[auth]
max_retries = 20
```

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `auth: retries exhausted`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.3

## What it means
The auth gave up after reaching the configured maximum number of retry attempts.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Check the logs for the underlying failure first. If the failures are transient, increase `auth.max_retries`.

Title: PaderQueue 1.1 release notes
Type: changelog

option `retention.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period starts throttling. - New error code PQ-E1547 (PARTITIONER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `partitioner.enabled`: turns the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written on or off.

- New option `scheduler.log_level`: log verbosity of the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time.

- New option `quota.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E4798 (SCHEDULER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `acktracker.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `snapshotter.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues.

- New error code PQ-E4663 (COORDINATOR_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `auth.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the authentication module that validates client tokens.

- New option `broker.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues.

- New error code PQ-E3805 (DLQ_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E2547 (COMPACTOR_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

# `acktracker.queue_capacity`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `5000` |
| Available since | 2.2 |
| Component | acktracker |
| Unit | tasks |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `acktracker.queue_capacity` only if you observe problems with the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[acktracker]
queue_capacity = 5000
```

# Postmortem INC-2025-131: chat-relay degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 40 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `chat-relay`

## Summary
During the incident, `chat-relay` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E4030 repeatedly.

## Timeline

- T+10: On-call engineer found PQ-E4030 in the broker logs.
- T+20: The team temporarily moved traffic to the secondary cluster.
- T+40: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a configuration change during a deployment.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E4030.
- Add an alert for this error code.

Title: PQ-E2547 COMPACTOR_COMPONENT_DISABLED
Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E2547 COMPACTOR_COMPONENT_DISABLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `compactor: component disabled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.1

## What it means
A request needed the compactor, but the compactor is switched off.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Enable the component by setting `compactor.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

# Postmortem INC-2025-182: notification-hub degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 210 minutes

showed error PQ-E3805 repeatedly.

- T+52: On-call engineer found PQ-E3805 in the broker logs.
- T+105: The team temporarily moved traffic to the secondary cluster.
- T+210: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E3805.
- Add an alert for this error code.

Title: PaderQueue 2.2 release notes

# PaderQueue 2.2 release notes

Released on 2022-12-12.

## New features

- New option `broker.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `acktracker.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed.

- New error code PQ-E4371 (ACKTRACKER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E4711 (ACKTRACKER_OPERATION_TIMEOUT) with a clearer log message.

- New option `snapshotter.log_level`: log verbosity of the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues.

- New error code PQ-E3828 (METRICS_CODEC_MISMATCH) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E3239 (QUOTA_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `coordinator.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers starts throttling.

- New option `coordinator.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers.

- New option `dlq.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue.

- New option `metrics.max_retries`: maximum number of retry attempts of the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics before an operation is reported as failed.

# PQ-E2425 ACKTRACKER_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `acktracker: retries exhausted`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 2.1

## What it means
The acktracker gave up after reaching the configured maximum number of retry attempts.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Check the logs for the underlying failure first. If the failures are transient, increase `acktracker.max_retries`.

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `compactor: component disabled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.1

## What it means
A request needed the compactor, but the compactor is switched off.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Enable the component by setting `compactor.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

- A deployment where nodes have different settings

# Postmortem INC-2025-153: user-activity degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 55 minutes
**Impact:** Delayed messages for `user-activity`

## Summary
During the incident, `user-activity` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E2451 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `user-activity` fired.
- T+13: On-call engineer found PQ-E2451 in the broker logs.
- T+27: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+55: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a configuration change during a deployment.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E2451.
- Add an alert for this error code.

[quota]

# PQ-E4895 REPLICATOR_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `replicator: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the replicator use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Set `replicator.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

# PQ-E2602 COORDINATOR_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `coordinator: work queue full`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.3

## What it means
The internal work queue of the coordinator is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- A long garbage collection pause
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `coordinator.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

# PQ-E3859 BROKER_OPERATION_TIMEOUT

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `broker: operation timeout`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 1.2

## What it means
An operation of the broker did not complete within the configured timeout.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Check network latency and load on the involved nodes. For slow but healthy clusters, increase `broker.timeout_ms`.

# PQ-E3859 BROKER_OPERATION_TIMEOUT

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `broker: operation timeout`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 1.2

## What it means
An operation of the broker did not complete within the configured timeout.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Check network latency and load on the involved nodes. For slow but healthy clusters, increase `broker.timeout_ms`.

# Postmortem INC-2024-141: billing-events degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 140 minutes
**Impact:** Delayed messages for `billing-events`

## Summary
During the incident, `billing-events` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E3859 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `billing-events` fired.
- T+35: On-call engineer found PQ-E3859 in the broker logs.
- T+70: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+140: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a configuration change during a deployment.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E3859.
- Add an alert for this error code.

Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E3891 COMPACTOR_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `compactor: work queue full`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
The internal work queue of the compactor is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `compactor.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

# PQ-E1441 COORDINATOR_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `coordinator: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the coordinator use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Set `coordinator.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

# `dlq.max_connections`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `64` |
| Available since | 2.0 |
| Component | dlq |
| Unit | connections |

## Notes

Changes to `dlq.max_connections` take effect after restarting the node. In clusters, use the same value on all nodes.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[dlq]
max_connections = 64
```

Type: error

# PQ-E2547 COMPACTOR_COMPONENT_DISABLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `compactor: component disabled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.1

## What it means
A request needed the compactor, but the compactor is switched off.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Enable the component by setting `compactor.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

# PQ-E2425 ACKTRACKER_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `acktracker: retries exhausted`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 2.1

## What it means
The acktracker gave up after reaching the configured maximum number of retry attempts.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Check the logs for the underlying failure first. If the failures are transient, increase `acktracker.max_retries`.

# PQ-E4157 REPLICATOR_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `replicator: buffer exhausted`
**Severity:** warning
**First introduced in:** 2.3

## What it means
The in-memory buffer of the replicator is full and new data is rejected.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Reduce the incoming rate or increase `replicator.buffer_bytes`. Also check whether downstream processing is stuck.

# PQ-E4020 SPOOL_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `spool: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.2

## What it means
Two nodes of the spool use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Set `spool.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

Title: PaderQueue 1.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 1.1

option `retention.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period starts throttling. - New error code PQ-E1547 (PARTITIONER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `partitioner.enabled`: turns the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written on or off.

- New option `scheduler.log_level`: log verbosity of the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time.

- New option `quota.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E4798 (SCHEDULER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `acktracker.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `snapshotter.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues.

- New error code PQ-E4663 (COORDINATOR_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `auth.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the authentication module that validates client tokens.

- New option `broker.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues.

- New error code PQ-E3805 (DLQ_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E2547 (COMPACTOR_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

# Postmortem INC-2024-136: report-builder degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 12 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `report-builder`

## Summary
During the incident, `report-builder` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E2758 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `report-builder` fired.
- T+3: On-call engineer found PQ-E2758 in the broker logs.
- T+6: The team restarted the affected nodes.
- T+12: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E2758.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# `partitioner.compression`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Compression codec that the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written uses for stored or transferred data.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | enum: none | lz4 | zstd |
| Default | `none` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Default changed | in 4.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `partitioner.compression` only if you observe problems with the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
compression = "none"
```

# PQ-E1944 RETENTION_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `retention: work queue full`
**Severity:** warning
**First introduced in:** 2.2

## What it means
The internal work queue of the retention is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- A long garbage collection pause
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `retention.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

# PQ-E3828 METRICS_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `metrics: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.2

## What it means
Two nodes of the metrics use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- A long garbage collection pause
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Set `metrics.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

# PaderQueue 1.1 release notes

Released on 2021-07-19.

## New features

- New option `scheduler.batch_size`: number of messages the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time processes together in one batch.

- New option `metrics.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics.

- New option `snapshotter.enabled`: turns the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues on or off.

- New option `auth.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the authentication module that validates client tokens waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `dlq.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `partitioner.max_retries`: maximum number of retry attempts of the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written before an operation is reported as failed.

- New error code PQ-E1616 (PARTITIONER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `replicator.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes.

- New option `retention.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period starts throttling.

- New error code PQ-E1547 (PARTITIONER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

**Severity:** warning
**First introduced in:** 1.2

Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E3642 ACKTRACKER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `acktracker: work queue full`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
The internal work queue of the acktracker is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `acktracker.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

Title: Postmortem INC-2025-118
Type: incident
Version: 4.x

# Postmortem INC-2025-118: checkout-service degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 25 minutes
**Impact:** Delayed messages for `checkout-service`

## Summary
During the incident, `checkout-service` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E3642 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `checkout-service` fired.
- T+6: On-call engineer found PQ-E3642 in the broker logs.
- T+12: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+25: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a configuration change during a deployment.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E3642.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# PQ-E2051 COMPACTOR_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `compactor: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the compactor use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- A slow disk
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Set `compactor.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

# PQ-E4798 SCHEDULER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `scheduler: buffer exhausted`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.1

## What it means
The in-memory buffer of the scheduler is full and new data is rejected.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Reduce the incoming rate or increase `scheduler.buffer_bytes`. Also check whether downstream processing is stuck.

# PQ-E3642 ACKTRACKER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `acktracker: work queue full`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
The internal work queue of the acktracker is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `acktracker.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

|---|---|

pq snapshot restore orders --retain-days
```

# Postmortem INC-2025-220: inventory-sync degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 25 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `inventory-sync`

## Summary
During the incident, `inventory-sync` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E4875 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `inventory-sync` fired.
- T+6: On-call engineer found PQ-E4875 in the broker logs.
- T+12: The team rolled back the last client deployment.
- T+25: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E4875.
- Add an alert for this error code.

- A consumer that stopped reading

Enable the component by setting `partitioner.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

**Log message:** `snapshotter: component disabled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.0

## What it means
A request needed the snapshotter, but the snapshotter is switched off.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Enable the component by setting `snapshotter.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

# `partitioner.enabled`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Turns the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written on or off.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | boolean |
| Default | `true` |
| Available since | 1.1 |
| Component | partitioner |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `partitioner.enabled` only if you observe problems with the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
enabled = true
```

Title: PaderQueue 1.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 1.1

option `retention.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period starts throttling. - New error code PQ-E1547 (PARTITIONER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `partitioner.enabled`: turns the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written on or off.

- New option `scheduler.log_level`: log verbosity of the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time.

- New option `quota.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E4798 (SCHEDULER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `acktracker.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `snapshotter.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues.

- New error code PQ-E4663 (COORDINATOR_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `auth.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the authentication module that validates client tokens.

- New option `broker.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues.

- New error code PQ-E3805 (DLQ_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E2547 (COMPACTOR_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

[partitioner]

# Postmortem INC-2025-173: shipping-tracker degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 90 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `shipping-tracker`

## Summary
During the incident, `shipping-tracker` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E4540 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `shipping-tracker` fired.
- T+22: On-call engineer found PQ-E4540 in the broker logs.
- T+45: The team temporarily moved traffic to the secondary cluster.
- T+90: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a configuration change during a deployment.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E4540.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# PQ-E2995 QUOTA_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `quota: retries exhausted`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
The quota gave up after reaching the configured maximum number of retry attempts.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- Too many tenants on one node

## How to fix
Check the logs for the underlying failure first. If the failures are transient, increase `quota.max_retries`.

Title: PaderQueue 1.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 1.1

# PaderQueue 1.1 release notes

Released on 2021-07-19.

## New features

- New option `scheduler.batch_size`: number of messages the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time processes together in one batch.

- New option `metrics.max_connections`: maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the metrics exporter that exposes Prometheus metrics.

- New option `snapshotter.enabled`: turns the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues on or off.

- New option `auth.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the authentication module that validates client tokens waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `dlq.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the dead-letter handler that moves undeliverable messages to the dead-letter queue waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `partitioner.max_retries`: maximum number of retry attempts of the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written before an operation is reported as failed.

- New error code PQ-E1616 (PARTITIONER_WORK_QUEUE_FULL) with a clearer log message.

- New option `replicator.worker_threads`: number of worker threads used by the replicator that copies partitions to follower nodes.

- New option `retention.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period starts throttling.

- New error code PQ-E1547 (PARTITIONER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

# PQ-E4590 SNAPSHOTTER_THROTTLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `snapshotter: throttled`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.1

## What it means
The snapshotter is throttling requests because usage is above the configured threshold.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Throttling protects the node. Add capacity or reduce load. As a last resort, raise `snapshotter.threshold_percent`.

Version: 4.x

# Postmortem INC-2024-119: user-activity degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 90 minutes
**Impact:** Duplicate processing in `user-activity`

## Summary
During the incident, `user-activity` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E4590 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `user-activity` fired.
- T+22: On-call engineer found PQ-E4590 in the broker logs.
- T+45: The team temporarily moved traffic to the secondary cluster.
- T+90: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a failing disk on one node.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E4590.
- Add an alert for this error code.

# PQ-E2051 COMPACTOR_CODEC_MISMATCH

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `compactor: codec mismatch`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
Two nodes of the compactor use different compression codecs and cannot read each other's data.

## Common causes
- A slow disk
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Set `compactor.compression` to the same value on all nodes, then restart them one after another.

# PQ-E3108 SPOOL_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `spool: connection limit reached`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.1

## What it means
The spool refused a new connection because the connection limit is reached.

## Common causes
- A long garbage collection pause
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Check for connection leaks in clients (connections that are never closed). If the load is legitimate, increase `spool.max_connections`.

Reduce the incoming rate or increase `acktracker.buffer_bytes`. Also check whether downstream processing is stuck.

# `retention.queue_capacity`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `10000` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | retention |
| Unit | tasks |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `retention.queue_capacity` only if you observe problems with the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[retention]
queue_capacity = 10000
```

Title: PQ-E4371 ACKTRACKER_COMPONENT_DISABLED
Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E4371 ACKTRACKER_COMPONENT_DISABLED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `acktracker: component disabled`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 2.2

## What it means
A request needed the acktracker, but the acktracker is switched off.

## Common causes
- A long garbage collection pause
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Enable the component by setting `acktracker.enabled` to `true` and restart the node.

Title: Postmortem INC-2025-204
Type: incident
Version: 4.x

# Postmortem INC-2025-204: report-builder degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 12 minutes
**Impact:** Duplicate processing in `report-builder`

## Summary
During the incident, `report-builder` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E4371 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `report-builder` fired.
- T+3: On-call engineer found PQ-E4371 in the broker logs.
- T+6: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+12: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a marketing campaign that tripled traffic.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E4371.
- Add an alert for this error code.

Title: spool.max_connections
Type: config
Version: 4.x

# `spool.max_connections`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `1024` |
| Available since | 2.1 |
| Component | spool |
| Unit | connections |
| Default changed | in 3.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `spool.max_connections` only if you observe problems with the on-disk spool that buffers incoming messages before they are written to segments, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[spool]
max_connections = 1024
```

Title: PQ-E3108 SPOOL_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED
Type: error
Version: 4.x

# PQ-E3108 SPOOL_CONNECTION_LIMIT_REACHED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `spool: connection limit reached`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.1

## What it means
The spool refused a new connection because the connection limit is reached.

## Common causes
- A long garbage collection pause
- Too small limits for the current load

## How to fix
Check for connection leaks in clients (connections that are never closed). If the load is legitimate, increase `spool.max_connections`.

Version: 4.x

# `scheduler.max_connections`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Maximum number of simultaneous client connections accepted by the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `64` |
| Available since | 2.1 |
| Component | scheduler |
| Unit | connections |

## Tuning advice

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `scheduler.max_connections` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[scheduler]
max_connections = 64
```

# `coordinator.batch_size` (PaderQueue 3.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Number of messages the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers processes together in one batch.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `500` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | coordinator |
| Unit | messages |

## Notes

Changes to `coordinator.batch_size` take effect after restarting the node. In clusters, use the same value on all nodes.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[coordinator]
batch_size = 500
```

# `coordinator.batch_size`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Number of messages the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers processes together in one batch.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `64` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | coordinator |
| Unit | messages |
| Default changed | in 4.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `coordinator.batch_size` only if you observe problems with the consumer group coordinator that assigns partitions to consumers, for example in the metrics dashboard.

[coordinator]

# PQ-E2425 ACKTRACKER_RETRIES_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `acktracker: retries exhausted`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 2.1

## What it means
The acktracker gave up after reaching the configured maximum number of retry attempts.

## Common causes
- A misconfigured client
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Check the logs for the underlying failure first. If the failures are transient, increase `acktracker.max_retries`.

# PQ-E2154 QUOTA_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `quota: work queue full`
**Severity:** critical
**First introduced in:** 3.0

## What it means
The internal work queue of the quota is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- Network problems between nodes
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `quota.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

Title: Postmortem INC-2024-103
Type: incident

# Postmortem INC-2024-103: search-indexer degraded

> Internal incident report

**Duration:** 90 minutes
**Impact:** Failed requests in `search-indexer`

## Summary
During the incident, `search-indexer` could not process messages reliably. The PaderQueue logs on the affected nodes
showed error PQ-E1584 repeatedly.

## Timeline
- T+0: Alerts for `search-indexer` fired.
- T+22: On-call engineer found PQ-E1584 in the broker logs.
- T+45: The team paused the noisiest producer.
- T+90: Service recovered.

## Root cause
The immediate trigger was a new client version with a retry bug.

## Follow-up
- The workaround is not a permanent fix. Apply the fix recommended in the error catalogue for PQ-E1584.
- Add an alert for this error code.

| Type | integer |

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[retention]
worker_threads = 2
```

# PQ-E3682 REPLICATOR_WORK_QUEUE_FULL

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `replicator: work queue full`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 2.0

## What it means
The internal work queue of the replicator is full, new tasks are rejected.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- A consumer that stopped reading

## How to fix
Add worker threads or increase `replicator.queue_capacity`. A queue that stays full usually means the component is too slow.

# PQ-E4798 SCHEDULER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED

> Error catalogue, PaderQueue 4.x

**Log message:** `scheduler: buffer exhausted`
**Severity:** error
**First introduced in:** 1.1

## What it means
The in-memory buffer of the scheduler is full and new data is rejected.

## Common causes
- A sudden spike in traffic
- A deployment where nodes have different settings

## How to fix
Reduce the incoming rate or increase `scheduler.buffer_bytes`. Also check whether downstream processing is stuck.

- Too many tenants on one node

Check network latency and load on the involved nodes. For slow but healthy clusters, increase `quota.timeout_ms`.

Title: PaderQueue 1.1 release notes
Type: changelog
Version: 1.1

option `retention.threshold_percent`: usage level in percent at which the retention manager that deletes messages older than the retention period starts throttling. - New error code PQ-E1547 (PARTITIONER_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `partitioner.enabled`: turns the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written on or off.

- New option `scheduler.log_level`: log verbosity of the scheduler that releases delayed messages at their due time.

- New option `quota.buffer_bytes`: size of the in-memory buffer used by the quota manager that limits the throughput per tenant, in bytes.

- New error code PQ-E4798 (SCHEDULER_BUFFER_EXHAUSTED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `acktracker.timeout_ms`: time in milliseconds that the acknowledgement tracker that records which messages consumers have confirmed waits for a response before the operation fails.

- New option `snapshotter.queue_capacity`: maximum number of pending tasks in the internal work queue of the snapshotter that creates point-in-time backups of queues.

- New error code PQ-E4663 (COORDINATOR_THROTTLED) with a clearer log message.

- New option `auth.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the authentication module that validates client tokens.

- New option `broker.interval_s`: interval in seconds between two background runs of the broker process that accepts messages from producers and routes them to queues.

- New error code PQ-E3805 (DLQ_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.

- New error code PQ-E2547 (COMPACTOR_COMPONENT_DISABLED) with a clearer log message.
